sensory.aromaNotes: Sulfur/garlic and fermented notes from mycelial cultures, especially when methionine is fed; fruiting bodies share the Tuber sulfur-volatile signature
sensory.meatAnalogRationale: Not a bulk protein or fibrous analog. Relevant as a mycelial flavor system: axenic T. borchii cultures produce human-detectable truffle aroma (Ehrlich-pathway sulfur volatiles). Related Tuber fruiting bodies also yield umami peptides studied for clean-label flavor. Do not treat fruiting-body harvest as a scalable protein ingredient.
sensory.preparationContext: Culinary fruiting bodies (mycorrhizal, orchard-grown or wild); R&D path is submerged/solid-state mycelium for aroma, not meat texture
sensory.confidenceNotes: 0–5 axes are a curator synthesis. Published rows below are GC-MS identifications from Mustafa et al. (2020) and Vahdatzadeh & Splivallo (2018), not converted panel scores.

publishedEvidence.name: 2-Methyl-4,5-dihydrothiophene and 3-methyl-4,5-dihydrothiophene
publishedEvidence.notes: Reported as species-characteristic thiophene derivatives and important contributors to the human-sensed bianchetto aroma.

publishedEvidence.name: Dimethyl sulfide, 2-methylbutanal, 3-methylbutanal, 1-octen-3-ol
publishedEvidence.sample: White and black Tuber species including T. borchii
publishedEvidence.notes: Common across most Tuber species; not unique to bianchetto.

publishedEvidence.name: Ehrlich-pathway Strecker aldehydes (2-methylbutanal and related C5 alcohols)
publishedEvidence.method: GC-MS of axenic mycelium; methionine feeding
publishedEvidence.notes: Mycelium produces human-detectable truffle aroma; methionine increases sulfur volatiles. This is the published R&D path for flavor without fruiting bodies.

morphology.fruitingBodyStructure: Hypogeous ascoma (truffle) with gleba and pale peridium; ectomycorrhizal, not a gilled mushroom
morphology.microscopyNotes: Food-flavor R&D uses vegetative mycelium in axenic culture, not the ascoma

nutrition.preparationContext: Fruiting-body proximate values vary widely; mycelial flavor biomass is not a protein ingredient
nutrition.confidenceNotes: Protein is not the use-case. Do not use these figures for formulation specs.

geographic.cultivatedRegions: European truffle orchards; mycelial flavor cultures in the lab
geographic.habitat: Ectomycorrhizal on oaks and other hosts; ascomata subterranean

strains.availabilityNotes: Flavor work uses axenic T. borchii isolates; add a verified accession before citing a catalog number.

commercialUse.applicationSummary: Culinary truffle and a documented mycelial source of natural truffle aroma (patents and strain-selection papers). Alt-protein role is flavor (umami / sulfur meaty notes), not fibrous protein. Black truffle (T. melanosporum) is the larger culinary market; T. borchii is the species with the strongest published mycelial-aroma data.

companies.name: European truffle orchards / mycelial aroma research groups

commercialUse.confidenceNotes: Flavor adjunct, not a meat analog biomass.

regulatory.notes: Traditional culinary ascomata. Mycelial aroma preparations would need their own composition and labeling review.

altProteinResearch.title: Improving truffle mycelium flavour through strain selection targeting volatiles of the Ehrlich pathway
altProteinResearch.summary: Axenic T. borchii mycelium produces human-detectable truffle aroma; methionine feeding increases sulfur volatiles. This is the main published path for truffle flavor without harvesting fruiting bodies.
